opennyai_summary.arguments: It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the first information report has been lodged making false allegations.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is further submitted that by impugned order applicants have been summoned for offence under Sections - 420, 406, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and as per law laid down in case of Delhi Race Club (1940) Ltd. and Others Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another;
2024 SCC Online SC 2248, the offence of cheating viz-a-viz criminal breach of trust are independent and distinct and both cannot exist simultaneously and on this account alone the impugned summoning order is liable to be set aside.
4. Perusal of record shows that by impugned order dated 07.03.2020, the applicants have been summoned under Sections - 420, 406, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C.
As stated above, in case of Delhi Race Club (supra), it has been held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that the offence of cheating viz-a-viz criminal breach of trust are independent and distinct and thus, the same cannot exist simultaneously in same set of facts and that they are antithetical to each other.
Thus, it is clear that impugned summoning order is not in accordance with law.
opennyai_summary.decision:
5. In view of the aforesaid, the impugned summoning order dated 07.03.2020, passed by the Special C.J.M., Kanpur Nagar is hereby set aside and the matter is remitted back to the court concerned to pass the order on the point of summoning afresh, expeditiously in accordance with law.
6.
The application u/s 528 BNSS is finally disposed of in above terms.
